concepts.why: The patient has a history of discharge through the artificial ear canal and a fistula originating from the middle ear, which are characteristic of chronic suppurative otitis media.

The patient has a hyperintense lesion at the edge of the petrous bone and a 2-centimeter mass found during drilling of the hypoplastic petrous bone, which are consistent with petrous bone osteomyelitis.
The patient has unilateral otomandibular syndrome and a fistula at the tip of the mastoid, which are characteristic of first branchial cleft anomaly.

The patient has a history of deep unilateral neck cellulitis and a millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle, which are consistent with sternocleidomastoid muscle abscess.

rationales.F06: Fistula originating from the middle ear suggests a connection between the middle ear and other structures, increasing the likelihood of chronic suppurative otitis media and petrous bone osteomyelitis.
rationales.F09: Millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle indicates a direct connection between the mastoid and the muscle, supporting the diagnosis of petrous bone osteomyelitis and sternocleidomastoid muscle abscess.
